newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican hog farmers anticipate rise in consumption.
newsitem.headline: Mexican hog farmers anticipate rise in consumption.

text.p: Mexican pork consumption could rise significantly in 1997 and reactivate the sector, said Ricardo Jimenez Rubio, president of the Mexico's Hog Farmers Union.
"We hope to recover at least some 25 to 30 percent of consumer potential," Jimenez told Reuters, speaking for hog farmers in Jalisco, the principal pork-producing state in Mexico.
"It is likely that by the end of the year we will produce close to 12 million (pigs)," he added.
In 1996, national production was close to nine million pigs, and Jimenez said the higher 1997 forecast is owed to expected greater consumption, lower grain prices and new markets.

He said in 1996 Mexican hog farmers incorporated new technology and genetics in the production of pork meat, which allowed the industry to boost its national presence in 1997 and establish the bases for exporting.
In the past a few hog farmers occassionally exported to Japan, but Jimenez said exports could be more consistent once some diseases that limit exports are eradicated.
The union of hog farmers also plans to engage in a publicity campaign to promote pork consumption.
